routine.intro: The routine is your daily checklist. It runs itself once a day — the writing stays yours.
routine.autoHint: At the scheduled time the app fetches today's challenge, creates the draft file, and signs in + claims every daily reward. Set it once and forget it.
routine.autoEnabled: Run the routine automatically every day
routine.autoMedium: Publish the draft to Medium (as a draft you can review)
routine.stepsHint: Switch off the steps you never use so the list stays short.
routine.extrasHint: Anything else you repeat daily (e.g. "check the group feed").
routine.checkInHint: One entry per account (e.g. 3 accounts on the same site). Only the URL and a Vault login are needed: the app finds the claim button and the login fields itself. "Check setup" signs in but never claims, so nothing is clicked twice.

dashboard.title: Home
dashboard.subtitle: Centralized automation for credentials, providers and scheduled tasks
dashboard.trayHint: Closing the window keeps TaskOrbit running in the system tray — right-click the ◈ icon for quick actions.
dashboard.encryptionWarn: OS encryption unavailable — key stored locally

vault.title: Credential Vault
vault.subtitle: Encrypted storage for provider credentials (AES-256-GCM)
vault.emptyHint: Add your first credential to get started
vault.confirmDeleteProvider: Delete this provider and ALL its credentials?
vault.backupHint: Export encrypts the entire vault (including secrets) with a passphrase of your choice (scrypt + AES-256-GCM). Keep the passphrase safe — there is no recovery.
vault.editHint: Leave the secret empty to keep the current one.
vault.securityHint: Reveal and copy stay available, but secrets are hidden again and the clipboard is wiped automatically (configurable in Settings › Security).

opencode.title: OpenCode Providers
opencode.subtitle: Providers detected in your OpenCode configuration
opencode.configMissingHint: Expected at the path below. It is created automatically by OpenCode.
opencode.configInvalid: Config file is not valid JSON
opencode.addHint: Writes the provider entry directly into your opencode config file (a timestamped backup is created first). OpenCode picks it up on next restart.
opencode.apiKeyHint: Stored in plaintext in the config file, exactly like a manually configured provider.
opencode.presetNoOpencode: Preset has no "opencode" section — only the automation config was loaded
opencode.presetLoadedReview: Preset loaded — review the details below, then click "Write to OpenCode config". Nothing is saved until you do.
opencode.automationDone: Automation finished — verify the result on the target site

automation.modelsToAdd: Models to add (each entry = one "Add Model" round)
automation.running: Running… the browser window stays open for review
automation.templateNote: Selectors are prefilled from the default OpenAI-compatible template — adjust them to match the target page.
automation.noModels: No model entries — only base fields will be filled
automation.presetLoaded: Preset loaded — review the filled form below, then click Run. Nothing is added until you run it.
automation.presetNoAutomation: Preset has no "automation" section — only the OpenCode provider data was loaded
automation.alsoWriteOpencode: Also add provider to OpenCode after run
automation.writeOpencodeDone: Provider written to the OpenCode config: {{path}} — restart OpenCode to pick it up

tasks.noTasks: No tasks match the current configuration — add watchers or check-ins in Settings
tasks.descDailyRoutine: Scaffolds today's draft, claims every daily reward and can publish the draft
tasks.descLeetcode: Polls the LeetCode GraphQL API, notifies and auto-opens new daily challenges
tasks.descWatcherHash: Notifies when the content of {{url}} changes
tasks.descWatcherGmail: Notifies for each new email in the Gmail label feed {{url}}
tasks.descCheckIn: Runs configured check-in requests sequentially, staggered minutes apart

autoclick.title: Auto Clicker
autoclick.subtitle: Automatic mouse clicking on any application — F6 toggles it from anywhere
autoclick.methodHint: Virtual clicks the window directly, so your real mouse is free to use (a small marker shows where it clicks). The window is locked when you press Start, so opening another browser over the point no longer steals the clicks. If a game/custom widget ignores it, switch to System mode.
autoclick.systemWarning: System mode takes over your real mouse — the window under the pointer cannot be used while it clicks. Use Virtual for browsers.
autoclick.yieldForeground: Pause while the target window is in front (use it freely)
autoclick.yieldHint: To use the same browser window while the clicker runs, enable the pause option above: clicks stop when that window is in front and resume when you switch away. To keep clicking while you browse, use a second browser/window — the locked target keeps receiving the clicks.
autoclick.pickMode: Pick a point on screen (click it after Start)
autoclick.routePoints: Route points ({{count}}) — clicked in order, then loops
autoclick.routeEmpty: No points yet — press Start and click each point, then press Esc
autoclick.routePickingHint: Click each point in order (they are added one by one). Press Esc when done — clicking starts automatically.
autoclick.routeFlowHint: After Start the app minimizes — click each point of the route in order, then press Esc to start clicking through them.
autoclick.startRoute: Start — click points, Esc to run
autoclick.extremeWarning: extreme speed — may destabilize some apps
autoclick.hotkeySaved: Hotkey set to {{key}} — works from any application
autoclick.repeatHint: Leave both limits at 0 to keep clicking until you stop it
autoclick.startPick: Start — then click the target point
autoclick.pickFlowHint: After Start the app minimizes — click anywhere on screen to pick the auto-click point. Esc cancels, F6 stops while it runs.
autoclick.pickingHint: The app is minimized — click anywhere on screen to pick the auto-click point. Esc cancels, F6 stops later.
autoclick.stopHint: {{key}} stops it from any application. The app stays minimized while clicking.
autoclick.antiIdleHint: Prevents the display/system from sleeping while unattended (uses Windows execution state, no mouse movement needed). Toggle on when waiting for tasks.

tabclick.title: Tab auto click (background)
tabclick.hint: Click tab A while you keep using tab B in the same window. Runs through the DevTools protocol, so clicks stay inside tab A and never reach the tab you are using. Open the debug browser (Opera GX / Chrome / Edge) with its dedicated profile, sign in once, then pick the tab.
tabclick.noTabs: No page tabs found — open the site, then connect again
tabclick.chooseTab: Connect and choose a tab first
tabclick.launched: Opened {{browser}} with a debug port. Sign in, open the tab, then connect.
tabclick.pick: Pick the click point in tab A
tabclick.pickWaiting: Switch to "{{title}}" and click the exact point to auto-click (that click is swallowed, it will not activate the page).
tabclick.pickTimeout: Timed out waiting for the click — try again.
tabclick.running: clicking tab A in the background
tabclick.backgroundHint: Now switch to tab B and use it normally — clicks stay in tab A. The app keeps that page focused/active so background throttling does not block it. Close the debug browser when done; its debug port is local-only.

promptforge.title: PromptForge
promptforge.subtitle: Rewrite a rough prompt into a structured one, then chat with it — rules and plugins included.
promptforge.emptyTitle: Turn rough ideas into sharp prompts
promptforge.emptyDesc: Type a rough prompt below. PromptForge rewrites it with role, context, steps, output format and constraints, then sends it to the model in the same thread.
promptforge.sendHint: Enter to enhance · Shift+Enter for a new line
promptforge.noModifiers: No rules or plugins active in this chat
promptforge.needKey: Add an API key in PromptForge settings to start.
promptforge.replaceKey: Enter a new key to replace the saved one
promptforge.keyHint: Encrypted on this machine and only used by the main process to call your endpoint.
promptforge.enchanterModelHint: Leave empty to use the default model
promptforge.invalidKey: That API key was rejected by the endpoint.
promptforge.rulesHint: Rules are injected into both the rewrite and the chat system prompt. Tap ✓ to use a rule in the open chat.
promptforge.noRules: No rules yet — create one to steer the model.
promptforge.ruleInstruction: Instruction, e.g. Always write TypeScript with strict typing…
promptforge.enabledByDefault: Enabled by default for new chats
promptforge.selectRule: Select a rule to edit or create a new one
promptforge.pluginsHint: Plugins add prompt modifiers to the rewrite and the chat. Built-ins are read-only.
promptforge.selectPlugin: Select a plugin to view or create a custom one
promptforge.errorReply: The model did not answer — see the error above.
promptforge.autoFreeHint: Fetches the provider catalogue and defaults to OpenRouter's free router (openrouter/free), so you only need a key. Re-checks every 6 hours; if a model disappears, becomes paid or is rate-limited, another free model is used automatically.
promptforge.autoModelSwitched: That model is unavailable — switched to {{model}}

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Application configuration and security information
settings.securityDb: Credentials are stored in an SQLite database in the data directory.
settings.securityEnc: Secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM; the master key is protected by the OS keystore (DPAPI / Keychain).
settings.securityLogs: Secrets are never written to logs or error messages.
settings.languageHint: The whole interface switches instantly — no restart needed.
settings.appearanceHint: Theme and accent apply instantly and are remembered for next launch. Ctrl K opens the command palette.
settings.clipboardClearHint: After you copy a secret, the clipboard is wiped once this many seconds pass (0 = never clear). Only applies while TaskOrbit is running.
settings.autoHideHint: A revealed secret is masked again after 60 seconds so it does not stay on screen.
settings.logsHint: Plain-text log of everything the app did (scheduler runs, watcher errors, alerts). Secrets are never logged.
settings.alertsHint: Mirror watcher / LeetCode / check-in notifications to your phone: create a Discord webhook (Server Settings → Integrations) or a Telegram bot (@BotFather) + chat ID. The URL/token stay on this machine.
settings.remoteHint: Run a local web server so your phone (same Wi-Fi) can control the PC: start/stop the clicker, run tasks, LeetCode, send/receive notifications. Installable via Add to Home Screen. Only enable on a trusted network — it is protected by an access key.
settings.remoteQrEmpty: Generate a link first (toggle on above)
settings.remoteSteps: 1) Phone on same Wi-Fi 2) Scan QR or open the link 3) Browser menu → Add to Home Screen to install it like an app.
settings.watchersHint: Poll a URL and get notified when its content changes (hash-based). Use the Cookie option for logged-in pages like UserCrowd.
settings.gmailHint: Gmail mode: set the URL to https://mail.google.com/mail/feed/atom/<label> (e.g. your VIP label), enter your Gmail address, and store an App Password (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords) as a credential in the Vault.
settings.watcherTestBaseline: Reachable — baseline recorded (first check never notifies)
settings.watcherTestUnchanged: Reachable — content unchanged since the last check
settings.watcherTestChanged: Content CHANGED since the last check
settings.watcherTestKeywordAbsent: Keyword is not on the page (will notify when it appears)
settings.watcherTestNotifyYes: · a real run would notify you
settings.checkInsHint: HTTP requests run as a staggered batch (default 3 minutes apart). Optionally authenticated with a Bearer token from a Vault credential.
